insight.title: Why You Catch Up Faster by Slowing Down
insight.subtitle: How reducing your speed helps you reach your goals sooner.

sections.text: To catch an object in orbit, you don’t aim at it and accelerate. You slow down. This drop in velocity lowers your altitude, which actually increases your speed relative to the earth below.

We treat deadlines like targets we must chase with force. But high-pressure acceleration clouds judgment. By lowering your intensity, you drop into a "lower orbit" where you can finally see the path clearly.
This is about efficiency, not laziness. When you stop rushing, you stop creating the mistakes that usually slow you down. You reach the destination sooner simply by refusing to chase it recklessly.
Try this today: When you feel rushed to finish a task today, pause for ten seconds to check your direction.
True speed is the absence of unnecessary friction.

news.title: Trump's Brinkmanship: A Two-Week Ceasefire and Market Reactions
news.description: U.S. President Donald Trump agreed to a two-week ceasefire with Iran, preventing military escalation and affecting global markets. The temporary truce aims to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, crucial for Gulf oil and gas exports. Investor reactions are mixed, citing uncertainties over oil prices and potential inflation.
news.why: Global safety risks are easing, reducing the chance of sudden travel disruptions.

news.title: Iran-US Ceasefire Triggers One Of Oil's Largest Single-Day Crashes In History, Crude Down 20%
news.description: $26 has been wiped from the price of a barrel in hours- the biggest single-day collapse since Covid destroyed global demand in April 2020.
news.why: Your daily commute and fuel bills are set to drop significantly.

news.title: Inflation poised to rise as sentiment weakens
news.description: Headline inflation is projected to rise in April for the first time in over a year, or since March 2025, while the consumer confidence index (CCI) fell sharply in March. Both are largely influenced by the Middle East conflict and rising energy prices, according to the Trade Policy and Strategy Office (TPSO).
news.why: You will likely pay more for groceries and essentials starting next month.

news.title: Skymet predicts below-normal monsoon in India this year; El Niño to hit second half
news.description: India anticipates below-normal monsoon rains in 2026. El Nino is expected to affect precipitation in the latter half of the season. This forecast raises concerns for crop production and overall inflation. While early, the prediction highlights potential challenges for the agricultural sector and the economy. Official forecasts are due next week.
news.why: Lower crop yields could drive up your monthly kitchen grocery bills.
